title: Porsche 918 vs LaFerrari: The Difference Nobody Explains

scenes.text: The Porsche nine eighteen Spyder and the Ferrari LaFerrari arrived within months of each other in twenty thirteen, both hybrids, both limited, both the fastest road cars their makers had ever built. But the numbers show two very different ideas of what a hybrid hypercar should be. One leans on its electric motors, the other on a huge V12. Here is the comparison, side by side, with every figure sourced.
scenes.caption: PORSCHE 918 vs LAFERRARI: THE DIFFERENCE NOBODY EXPLAINS

scenes.text: We use Wikipedia's pages for both cars, Porsche's own press release, evo, Motorious, Sotheby's, RM Sotheby's, Broad Arrow and the duPont Registry. Where a figure is a manufacturer claim, we say so. Where two sources disagree, we show both. And where we compare numbers measured in different units or on different tracks, we warn you before we do the sum.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: WIKIPEDIA · PORSCHE PRESS RELEASE (COMPANY SOURCE) · EVO · MOTORIOUS · SOTHEBY'S · RM SOTHEBY'S · BROAD ARROW · DUPONT REGISTRY

scenes.text: Evo's Harry Metcalfe calls the nine eighteen, the McLaren P1 and the LaFerrari the first plug-in hybrid supercars, and the Holy Trinity. He says the Porsche is the cleverest and technically the most impressive. Of the Ferrari, he says its naturally aspirated V12 is the focus: the electric motor never seems to help, and the car feels as if the engine had been enlarged to ten litres.
scenes.caption: METCALFE (EVO): 918 'THE CLEVEREST AND TECHNICALLY THE MOST IMPRESSIVE' · LAFERRARI: ELECTRIC MOTOR 'NEVER SEEMS TO HELP' · FEELS LIKE A 10-LITRE ENGINE

scenes.text: That is one writer's opinion, and we label it as such. But the specification sheets support the contrast. The Porsche pairs a four point six litre V8 with two electric motors. The Ferrari pairs a six point three litre V12 with a single hybrid unit. The Porsche was built to use electricity as a core part of its performance. The Ferrari, on its numbers, uses it as a supplement.
scenes.caption: 918: 4.6 L V8 + 2 ELECTRIC MOTORS · LAFERRARI: 6.3 L V12 + 1 HY-KERS UNIT (WIKIPEDIA) · 'CORE vs SUPPLEMENT' IS OUR READING OF THE NUMBERS

scenes.text: Both were unveiled with fanfare. Wikipedia says the nine eighteen debuted as a concept at the Geneva Motor Show in March twenty ten and went into production on the eighteenth of September, twenty thirteen. The LaFerrari was shown at the twenty thirteen Geneva show. The name means the Ferrari in Italian, Wikipedia says, and was meant to be the definitive Ferrari. It succeeds the Enzo, and the F eighty is its successor.
scenes.caption: 918: CONCEPT MARCH 2010, PRODUCTION SEPT 18, 2013 · LAFERRARI: GENEVA 2013 · NAME = 'THE FERRARI' · SUCCEEDS THE ENZO; SUCCESSOR F80 (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: There is a styling footnote. Wikipedia says Pininfarina had no input in the LaFerrari's design. It was the first Ferrari since the nineteen seventy-three Dino three oh eight GT four without Pininfarina styling, ending a collaboration dating to nineteen fifty-one. By our arithmetic, that collaboration lasted about sixty-two years, so the LaFerrari marks a break in how Ferrari designs its cars.
scenes.caption: NO PININFARINA INPUT · FIRST FERRARI WITHOUT IT SINCE THE 1973 DINO 308 GT4 · COLLABORATION SINCE 1951 ≈ 62 YEARS (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Engines. The nine eighteen's four point six litre V8, Wikipedia says, makes six hundred eight metric horsepower at eighty-seven hundred rpm and five hundred forty newton-metres. The LaFerrari's six point three litre F one forty V12 makes eight hundred metric horsepower at nine thousand rpm and seven hundred newton-metres. By our arithmetic, the Ferrari's engine makes thirty-two percent more power than the Porsche's, and thirty percent more torque.
scenes.caption: 918 V8: 608 PS / 540 N·M · LAFERRARI V12: 800 PS / 700 N·M → +31.6% POWER · +29.6% TORQUE (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Per litre, the numbers reverse. By our arithmetic, six hundred eight over four point five nine three litres is about one hundred thirty-two metric horsepower per litre, and eight hundred over six point two six two is about one hundred twenty-eight. The smaller Porsche engine is slightly more efficient per litre, which fits Porsche's own claim that it is the highest of any naturally aspirated Porsche engine.
scenes.caption: 918: 608 ÷ 4.593 L ≈ 132 PS/L · LAFERRARI: 800 ÷ 6.262 L ≈ 128 PS/L (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Electric. Wikipedia lists the Porsche's two motors at one hundred fifteen and ninety-five kilowatts, two hundred ten kilowatts or two hundred eighty-six metric horsepower in total. The Ferrari's HY-KERS unit is one hundred sixty-three metric horsepower and provides short bursts of extra power. By our arithmetic, the Porsche's electric power is seventy-six percent greater than the Ferrari's, and makes up thirty-two percent of its system output, against seventeen percent for the Ferrari.
scenes.caption: 918: 210 KW (286 PS) = 32% OF 887 PS · LAFERRARI: 163 PS = 17% OF 963 PS · 286 vs 163 = +75.5% (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: System output. Wikipedia lists the nine eighteen at eight hundred eighty-seven metric horsepower and twelve hundred eighty newton-metres, and the LaFerrari at nine hundred sixty-three metric horsepower and nine hundred newton-metres. By our arithmetic, the Ferrari has eight point six percent more power, and the Porsche has forty-two percent more torque. RM Sotheby's, in a twenty twenty-six sale, gives the LaFerrari's output as nine hundred forty-nine horsepower, which is the same figure expressed differently.
scenes.caption: 918: 887 PS / 1,280 N·M · LAFERRARI: 963 PS / 900 N·M → FERRARI +8.6% POWER · PORSCHE +42.2% TORQUE (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC) · RM SOTHEBY'S: 949 HP FOR LAFERRARI

scenes.text: A check on that last point. Nine hundred sixty-three metric horsepower is nine hundred fifty mechanical horsepower, by our arithmetic, so RM Sotheby's nine hundred forty-nine is within one horsepower, a rounding difference. The Porsche's eight hundred eighty-seven metric is eight hundred seventy-five. So on the same basis, the Ferrari has seventy-five horsepower more, eight and a half percent.
scenes.caption: 963 PS = 950 HP · 887 PS = 875 HP → +75 HP (+8.6%) (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Revs. Wikipedia lists the Ferrari engine's peak power at nine thousand rpm. Porsche's release says its V8 can run to nine thousand one hundred fifty. So both engines are happy at very high revs, and both are naturally aspirated, which was unusual for hypercars then and is rarer now. The Ferrari uses twelve cylinders to get there, and the Porsche eight, and the sources do not say which sounds better.
scenes.caption: LAFERRARI PEAK POWER 9,000 RPM (WIKIPEDIA) · 918 UP TO 9,150 RPM (PORSCHE) · BOTH NATURALLY ASPIRATED

scenes.text: Weight. Wikipedia lists the LaFerrari with a claimed dry weight of about twelve hundred fifty-five kilograms and a kerb weight of fifteen hundred eighty-five. The nine eighteen's curb weight is sixteen hundred thirty-four to seventeen hundred twenty kilograms, Wikipedia says, and Porsche says about sixteen hundred forty with the Weissach package. By our arithmetic, the Porsche is forty-nine to one hundred thirty-five kilograms heavier than the Ferrari's kerb weight.
scenes.caption: LAFERRARI DRY ~1,255 KG · KERB 1,585 KG · 918 CURB 1,634–1,720 KG (~1,640 WITH WEISSACH) → +49 TO +135 KG vs LAFERRARI KERB (WIKIPEDIA, PORSCHE; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Power to weight. By our arithmetic, the LaFerrari's nine hundred fifty horsepower over a kerb weight of one point five eight five tonnes is about five hundred ninety-nine horsepower per tonne. The nine eighteen's eight hundred seventy-five over one point six four tonnes is about five hundred thirty-three. So the Ferrari leads on power to weight by about twelve percent, on these figures.
scenes.caption: LAFERRARI 950 ÷ 1.585 t ≈ 599 HP/t · 918 875 ÷ 1.64 t ≈ 533 HP/t → +12.4% FOR FERRARI (OUR ARITHMETIC; KERB/CURB WEIGHTS)

scenes.text: There is a catch. The two weight figures are not necessarily measured the same way. Kerb weight conventions differ, and the Ferrari's is listed on Wikipedia without a source we could check, while the Porsche's comes from Porsche's own release for the Weissach car. So the twelve percent is indicative. The sources do not give a weight for a standard-spec nine eighteen from Porsche, only a range from Wikipedia.
scenes.caption: KERB/CURB CONVENTIONS MAY DIFFER · LAFERRARI KERB WEIGHT UNSOURCED ON WIKIPEDIA · 918 FIGURE FROM PORSCHE'S WEISSACH SPEC

scenes.text: Acceleration. Wikipedia lists the LaFerrari at zero to one hundred kilometres per hour in two point six seconds and zero to two hundred in under six point nine. The nine eighteen's official zero to sixty is two point six, though Car and Driver measured two point two and Motor Trend two point four. Careful: sixty miles per hour is ninety-seven kilometres per hour, so the Porsche's time is for a slightly lower speed.
scenes.caption: LAFERRARI 0–100 KM/H 2.6 s · 0–200 UNDER 6.9 s · 918 0–60 MPH 2.6 s OFFICIAL (2.2 C/D, 2.4 MOTOR TREND) · 60 MPH = 96.6 KM/H (WIKIPEDIA; OUR CONVERSION)
scenes.chapter: Speed and the claims that failed

scenes.text: Now the claim that failed. Wikipedia says Ferrari's claim of zero to three hundred kilometres per hour in fifteen seconds was debunked, and the verified time is twenty-one point nine nine seconds. By our arithmetic, the verified time is six point nine nine seconds longer than claimed, or forty-seven percent. Wikipedia's McLaren P1 page lists that car's claim as sixteen point five. The sources do not name who verified the Ferrari time.
scenes.caption: CLAIMED 15 s → VERIFIED 21.99 s: +6.99 s (+46.6%) · P1 CLAIM 16.5 s (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC) · WHO VERIFIED: NOT NAMED IN OUR SOURCE

scenes.text: Top speed. Wikipedia says Ferrari states in excess of three hundred fifty kilometres per hour for the LaFerrari. The nine eighteen's official figure is three hundred forty-five, two hundred fourteen miles per hour, and an independent test reached three hundred fifty-two, two hundred eighteen point seven. By our arithmetic, that is within seven kilometres per hour, and since Ferrari only states in excess of three fifty, we cannot say which car is faster.
scenes.caption: LAFERRARI: 'IN EXCESS OF 350 KM/H' · 918: 345 KM/H OFFICIAL · 352 KM/H INDEPENDENT TEST (WIKIPEDIA) → NOT RESOLVABLE

scenes.text: Lap times. Wikipedia lists the LaFerrari's Fiorano lap, claimed by Ferrari, as one minute nineteen point seven. The nine eighteen's six fifty-seven is a Nordschleife time. These are two different tracks, so no comparison is possible, and we found no LaFerrari Nürburgring time in our sources. The sources compare cars on their own terms: Ferrari's home track, Porsche's famous lap.
scenes.caption: LAFERRARI FIORANO 1:19.70 (FERRARI CLAIM) · 918 NORDSCHLEIFE 6:57 · DIFFERENT TRACKS — NOT COMPARABLE · LAFERRARI NÜRBURGRING TIME: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Aerodynamics. Wikipedia says the LaFerrari's active aerodynamics are managed by twenty-one onboard computers, but gives no downforce figure for the road car. The Porsche's release describes Porsche Active Aerodynamics with three modes, a Race mode with a steep wing angle and extended spoiler, and underfloor flaps. Neither source gives a comparable downforce number, so we cannot compare the two on aero.
scenes.caption: LAFERRARI: ACTIVE AERO, 21 COMPUTERS, NO DOWNFORCE FIGURE · 918: PAA, 3 MODES, NO DOWNFORCE FIGURE IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Efficiency. Wikipedia lists the nine eighteen's carbon dioxide at seventy-nine grams per kilometre and three litres per hundred kilometres on the NEDC test, an electric range of nineteen kilometres under the EPA, and a total range of six hundred eighty kilometres. For the LaFerrari, Ferrari claims three hundred thirty grams per kilometre, and a forty percent reduction in fuel consumption, the source does not say compared with what.
scenes.caption: 918: 79 G/KM CO₂ (NEDC) · EV RANGE 19 KM (EPA) · TOTAL RANGE 680 KM · LAFERRARI: 330 G/KM CO₂ (FERRARI CLAIM) · '40% REDUCTION' — BASELINE NOT STATED (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the LaFerrari's claimed emissions are about four point two times the nine eighteen's. Both are NEDC-style claims, but the Porsche has a plug-in battery that the NEDC test rewards, and the Ferrari's HY-KERS unit does not appear to be plug-in. The sources do not say how the two were measured, so the ratio shows the difference in design more than in efficiency.
scenes.caption: 330 ÷ 79 ≈ 4.2× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · TEST BASIS NOT FULLY STATED — PLUG-IN vs NON-PLUG-IN DESIGN

scenes.text: The Ferrari's battery. Wikipedia does not state the LaFerrari's battery capacity, and the sources do not give an electric range. The Porsche's is a 6.8 kilowatt-hour pack. So here the comparison is simple: one car has a published battery size and an EPA electric range, and the other has neither in our sources. That alone shows a different attitude towards the electric part of the system.
scenes.caption: 918: 6.8 KWH, 19 KM EPA ELECTRIC RANGE · LAFERRARI: BATTERY SIZE AND EV RANGE NOT STATED IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Production. Wikipedia says the nine eighteen was limited to nine hundred eighteen units. The LaFerrari coupé was limited to four hundred ninety-nine units, with a five hundredth car auctioned for charity on the third of December, twenty sixteen, by RM Sotheby's for seven million dollars. The open-top Aperta had two hundred initially sold, nine reserved for the seventieth anniversary and one more auctioned: two hundred ten in all.
scenes.caption: 918: 918 UNITS · LAFERRARI COUPÉ: 499 + 500TH CAR ($7M, CHARITY, DEC 3, 2016) · APERTA: 200 + 9 + 1 = 210 (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the Porsche was built in a run 1.84 times as large as the LaFerrari coupé's. Counting all LaFerrari variants, the five hundred coupés and two hundred ten Apertas make seven hundred ten, so the Porsche run is still 1.29 times as large. Wikipedia says all two hundred Apertas were pre-sold to customers by invitation.
scenes.caption: 918 ÷ 499 = 1.84 · 918 ÷ 710 = 1.29 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · APERTA: ALL 200 PRE-SOLD BY INVITATION (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Price. Wikipedia says the nine eighteen started at about seven hundred eighty-one thousand euros in Europe, eight hundred forty-five thousand dollars in the United States and seven hundred eleven thousand pounds in Britain. It says only that each LaFerrari cost more than one million euros. By our arithmetic, one million over seven hundred eighty-one thousand is one point two eight, so the Ferrari cost at least twenty-eight percent more than the Porsche in Europe. The real gap could be larger, since our sources give no more precise LaFerrari price. The Porsche's Weissach package added eighty-four thousand dollars, and Sotheby's lists one LaFerrari with one hundred twenty-seven thousand, two hundred forty-one dollars in factory options.
scenes.caption: 918 ≈ €781,000 / $845,000 / £711,000 · LAFERRARI > €1,000,000 → AT LEAST ≈ +28% IN EUROPE; WEISSACH +$84,000; ONE LAFERRARI $127,241 IN OPTIONS (WIKIPEDIA, SOTHEBY'S; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The third car of the trinity, the McLaren P1, gives a useful midpoint. Wikipedia says three hundred seventy-five standard P1s were built, plus fifty-eight P1 GTRs, from October twenty thirteen to December twenty fifteen. Its three point eight litre twin-turbo V8 makes seven hundred thirty-seven metric horsepower and its electric motor one hundred seventy-nine, for nine hundred sixteen combined and nine hundred newton-metres.
scenes.caption: P1: 375 BUILT (+58 GTR) · OCT 2013 – DEC 2015 · 3.8 L TWIN-TURBO V8 737 PS + ELECTRIC 179 PS = 916 PS · 900 N·M (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the P1's system output of nine hundred sixteen sits between the Porsche's eight hundred eighty-seven and the Ferrari's nine hundred sixty-three. Its electric motor, at one hundred seventy-nine, is slightly stronger than the Ferrari's one hundred sixty-three, and well below the Porsche's two hundred eighty-six. Its torque matches the Ferrari's nine hundred, with the Porsche's twelve eighty far above both.
scenes.caption: SYSTEM: 918 887 · P1 916 · LAFERRARI 963 PS · ELECTRIC: 918 286 · P1 179 · LAFERRARI 163 PS · TORQUE: 918 1,280 · P1 900 · LAFERRARI 900 N·M (WIKIPEDIA; OUR COMPARISON)

scenes.text: Weight on the P1's page is inconsistent. The infobox lists a kerb weight of fourteen hundred ninety kilograms, the text gives fifteen hundred forty-seven, citing Autocar, and the dry weight is thirteen hundred ninety-five. Using the text figure, the P1 is lighter than the Ferrari's kerb weight of fifteen eighty-five by thirty-eight kilograms, and lighter than the Porsche's sixteen forty by ninety-three, by our arithmetic.
scenes.caption: P1: INFOBOX 1,490 KG · TEXT 1,547 KG (AUTOCAR) · DRY 1,395 KG · vs LAFERRARI KERB 1,585 (−38 KG) · vs 918 ~1,640 (−93 KG) (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Speed. Wikipedia lists the P1's zero to one hundred kilometres per hour at two point eight seconds and its zero to three hundred at sixteen point five seconds, McLaren's claims, with a top speed electronically limited to three hundred fifty kilometres per hour, two hundred seventeen miles per hour. The Ferrari's claimed fifteen seconds was quicker than McLaren's claim, but its verified twenty-one point nine nine was far slower. The Porsche's zero to three hundred is not given in our sources.
scenes.caption: P1: 0–100 KM/H 2.8 s · 0–300 KM/H 16.5 s (MCLAREN CLAIM) · LIMITED TO 350 KM/H (217 MPH) · 918 0–300: NOT IN OUR SOURCES (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Wikipedia also notes that McLaren announced a sub-seven-minute Nürburgring lap for the P1 without publishing the exact time, and that the six forty-three point two two time belongs to the P1 LM prototype in April twenty seventeen, which was not road legal during the run. So the P1's lap is the least documented of the three, and we do not rank it.
scenes.caption: P1: SUB-7-MINUTE LAP ANNOUNCED, TIME NOT PUBLISHED · 6:43.22 BELONGS TO THE P1 LM PROTOTYPE (APRIL 2017), NOT ROAD LEGAL (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: A word on reliability. Wikipedia says the nine eighteen has been the subject of half a dozen recalls, including issues with control arms and seat belts. It says eighty-five LaFerrari coupés from the twenty fourteen and twenty fifteen model years were recalled for headrest and tyre-pressure system issues. By our arithmetic, that is about seventeen percent of the four hundred ninety-nine coupés.
scenes.caption: 918: ~6 RECALLS (CONTROL ARMS, SEAT BELTS) · LAFERRARI: 85 COUPÉS RECALLED (HEADREST, TYRE-PRESSURE SYSTEM) = 17.0% OF 499 (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Service costs. Motorious, describing a delivery-mileage twenty fifteen LaFerrari to be sold at Broad Arrow's Zürich auction, says recent work at Rossocorsa, Ferrari's official dealer in Milan, included a new high-voltage battery and a fix for the sticky button switchgear issue, with an invoice above two hundred thousand euros. It says a buyer inherits a LaFerrari with its largest looming expense already covered.
scenes.caption: RECENT WORK AT ROSSOCORSA, MILAN: NEW HIGH-VOLTAGE BATTERY + 'STICKY BUTTON' FIX · INVOICE > €200,000 (MOTORIOUS)

scenes.text: That one article is the only LaFerrari service figure in our sources, and it is a single car's invoice. The car, Motorious says, had just ninety-two kilometres, was offered without reserve against an estimate of five and a half to seven and a half million Swiss francs, and had a special series Yellow Book documenting early ownership. We found no nine eighteen service invoice at all.
scenes.caption: CHASSIS 214333: 92 KM · NO RESERVE · EST. CHF 5.5M–7.5M · YELLOW BOOK (MOTORIOUS) · 918 SERVICE INVOICES: NONE FOUND

scenes.text: Resale. Sotheby's lists seven recent LaFerrari sales between February twenty twenty-five and January twenty twenty-six. A two thousand fifteen coupé with fifty-four miles and one hundred twenty-seven thousand dollars of options sold for five million, two hundred thirty thousand dollars in August twenty twenty-five. A two thousand fifteen coupé with one thousand nine hundred thirty-eight miles sold for five million, four hundred seventy-seven thousand, five hundred in January twenty twenty-six.
scenes.caption: 2015 COUPÉ (54 MI, $127,241 OPTIONS): $5,230,000, AUG 2025 · 2015 COUPÉ (1,938 MI): $5,477,500, JAN 2026 (SOTHEBY'S, RM SOTHEBY'S)

scenes.text: Others were lower. A two thousand fourteen LaFerrari delivered new to Kuwait with three thousand seven hundred one kilometres sold for three million, three hundred eighty thousand dollars in December twenty twenty-five. A twenty fourteen car in Grigio Ferro with sixteen hundred thirteen kilometres sold for three million, three hundred twenty-three thousand, seven hundred fifty Swiss francs in October. So coupés sold anywhere from about three to five and a half million.
scenes.caption: 2014 (KUWAIT, 3,701 KM): $3,380,000, DEC 2025 · 2014 (1,613 KM): CHF 3,323,750 (~$4.17M PER SOTHEBY'S TABLE), OCT 2025 (SOTHEBY'S)

scenes.text: The Aperta, the open-top car, sold for more. Sotheby's lists a two thousand seventeen Aperta at six million, seven hundred fifteen thousand dollars in August twenty twenty-five, with under twenty-three hundred miles. And Wikipedia says the last Aperta sold at auction in twenty seventeen for ten million dollars. Hagerty, per Motorious, lists a number three good-condition twenty fifteen LaFerrari at five million, six hundred fifty thousand, up seventy-three point eight percent in a year.
scenes.caption: APERTA $6,715,000 (AUG 2025) · LAST APERTA $10M (2017) · HAGERTY #3 (GOOD) 2015 LAFERRARI $5.65M, +73.8% IN ONE YEAR (SOTHEBY'S, WIKIPEDIA, MOTORIOUS)

scenes.text: And the Porsche. The duPont Registry reports a standard nine eighteen with four hundred twenty miles sold for two point nine six million in June twenty twenty-six, and a Weissach with twelve sixty-seven miles for four million six hundred eighty thousand in April, plus a one-of-one Pure Orange car for six point oh five million at Mecum in January. By our arithmetic, the LaFerrari coupé that sold for five point four seven eight million is about one point eight five times the standard nine eighteen's two point nine six. These are single sales with different mileage, so this is not a market index, but the gap is real in the sales we found.
scenes.caption: 918: $2.96M STANDARD · $4.68M WEISSACH · $6.05M RECORD · LAFERRARI COUPÉ $5.478M ≈ 1.85× THE STANDARD 918 (DUPONT REGISTRY, SOTHEBY'S; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: One more Ferrari detail. Wikipedia says the FXX-K Evo's downforce is twenty-three percent above the FXX-K's and seventy-five percent above the road car's. By our arithmetic, that implies the FXX-K, the track version, has about forty-two percent more downforce than the road car. The page gives no road-car downforce number, so these are ratios only, and we cannot convert them into kilograms.
scenes.caption: FXX-K EVO = 1.23× FXX-K = 1.75× ROAD CAR → FXX-K ≈ 1.42× ROAD CAR (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC) · NO ABSOLUTE DOWNFORCE FIGURE

scenes.text: The Aperta against the coupé. Sotheby's lists a two thousand seventeen Aperta at six million, seven hundred fifteen thousand dollars, and the highest coupé at five million, four hundred seventy-seven thousand, five hundred. By our arithmetic, the Aperta is twenty-three percent higher. The Aperta run is two hundred ten cars against four hundred ninety-nine coupés, a smaller run, though the cars differ in mileage and year as well.
scenes.caption: APERTA $6,715,000 vs COUPÉ $5,477,500 → +22.6% · 210 vs 499 UNITS (SOTHEBY'S, WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Hagerty's figure deserves a closer look. Motorious says Hagerty lists a number three, good condition, twenty fifteen LaFerrari at five million, six hundred fifty thousand dollars, up seventy-three point eight percent over the past year. By our arithmetic, that means the same valuation was about three point two five million a year earlier. That is consistent with several of the three-million-dollar sales in Sotheby's list.
scenes.caption: $5.65M ÷ 1.738 ≈ $3.25M A YEAR EARLIER (HAGERTY VIA MOTORIOUS; OUR ARITHMETIC) · SOTHEBY'S LIST INCLUDES SALES AT $3.38M–$4.17M

scenes.text: A caution about Sotheby's own table. The article's currency conversions do not always match its text, and for one car the text says three million, five hundred forty-eight thousand, seven hundred fifty euros while the table says three point six nine five million dollars. We therefore use the dollar sales that are stated plainly, and mark the converted ones. The article also gives no original price for any car.
scenes.caption: SOTHEBY'S TABLE: SOME CHF/EUR→USD CONVERSIONS DO NOT MATCH THE TEXT · NO ORIGINAL PRICES GIVEN · WE USE STATED USD SALES

scenes.text: The Porsche's most expensive sale is a different case. The duPont Registry says the one-of-one Pure Orange nine eighteen sold for six million, fifty thousand dollars at Mecum Kissimmee in January twenty twenty-six, beating a previous record of three million, nine hundred thirty-seven thousand, five hundred. By our arithmetic, the new record was fifty-four percent higher. A paint-to-sample car is the Porsche market's equivalent of the Aperta.
scenes.caption: $6,050,000 vs PREVIOUS RECORD $3,937,500 = +53.7% (DUPONT REGISTRY; OUR ARITHMETIC) · 'PAINT-TO-SAMPLE ≈ APERTA' IS OUR ANALOGY

scenes.text: What we could not find. A LaFerrari Nürburgring lap. The LaFerrari's battery size or electric range. Who verified the twenty-one point nine nine second zero to three hundred time. A downforce figure for either car. And a weight measured the same way for both. If you have a reliable source for any of them, share the link in the comments, and we will update the description.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: LAFERRARI NÜRBURGRING TIME · BATTERY/EV RANGE · VERIFIER OF 21.99 s · DOWNFORCE · SAME-BASIS WEIGHTS
scenes.chapter: What our sources do not say

scenes.text: So which is better? On the numbers: the Ferrari has more power and a lower weight, the Porsche has more torque, more electric power, a published battery, lower emissions, and a famous lap time. Evo's Metcalfe liked both, and called the Porsche the cleverest. The market currently values the LaFerrari more highly. That is a result, not a verdict.
scenes.caption: FERRARI: POWER, WEIGHT, RESALE · PORSCHE: TORQUE, ELECTRIC POWER, EMISSIONS, 6:57 LAP, LARGER RUN · MARKET: LAFERRARI HIGHER

scenes.text: Which one would you rather have? Tell us in the comments. In the other videos of this series, we reveal two secrets inside the Porsche nine eighteen, count what it really costs to own one, and tell the story of the hypercar holy trinity. Our twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked in the description. Subscribe to Pickup Reality.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY
